article.name: CSM
article.summary: CSM is a local and self-hosted memory and operational-continuity runtime for coding agents. Its layered system combines durable memory, project event history, re-entry context, context controls, and governance, with PostgreSQL for the complete feature path and a narrower SQLite core. This bounded review describes official documentation and selected source at the verified master head; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: CSM (Cross-Session Memory) is a source-first local/self-hosted agent memory and continuity runtime. Its documented surfaces span durable memory, AgentBook project activity, fresh-session re-entry, context management, Living State and governance.

GitHub identifies master as the default branch. The official master Atom feed and full commit page identify 9c7cfb22e525eb9210c3048cb0d44544b09b95d0 as its current head; the feed gives the commit time as 2026-09-18T00:21:00Z. Review time was 2026-11-25T10:14:30Z (UTC; 2026-11-25 02:14:30 PST, America/Los_Angeles).

architecture.text: The documented runtime is layered: host integration and provider-aware tool registration sit above storage, durable memory, AgentBook, re-entry, Living State, context control, work continuity and governance. PostgreSQL is the complete feature path; SQLite provides a local core and removes unsupported PostgreSQL-only tools at registration.

Durable memory handles saving and classification, text/vector retrieval, metadata filters, relationship traversal, lessons and transcript-derived records, compaction, embedding backfill, duplicate handling and maintenance. AgentBook separately stores append-only operational events and derives summaries, current state and a Markdown front page for project resumption.

At the memory layer, the manager persists typed memory records with metadata and embeddings and can create graph links; indexed search uses vector, full-text and entity candidates, then recency/weight scoring, rank fusion and content deduplication. The product architecture describes provider-specific availability rather than full PostgreSQL/SQLite parity.

behavior.text: Writes may arrive through host hooks or explicit tools. The architecture describes normalization and configured redaction, metadata/provenance construction, durable persistence, then embedding and relationship work where supported. The privacy document says automatic conversation and full-transcript capture default to enabled, so operators need to review capture settings before handling sensitive content.

Memory metadata is completed with source_kind, evidence_strength, source_session_id, source_agent_id, source_model_id and source_surface fields; a missing model identity is marked unknown. The read-only provenance audit counts incomplete fields and unknown/default model IDs across all and active rows.

Ordinary memory records can be updated through write/manage operations. The merge implementation groups active records with matching normalized content and memory type, marks duplicates superseded, and records a merge row; this is a non-destructive duplicate merge path rather than a general immutable edit history.

Direct deletion requires both memory ID and active project and hard-deletes the database record with dependent rows covered by foreign-key cascades. Retention cleanup is explicit and preview-first, project-bound and capped per application. These database operations do not erase copies in generated documents, exports, logs, snapshots, filesystem backups or third-party backups.

Hybrid recall launches vector, full-text and entity candidate retrieval in parallel, applies configured weights and recency scoring, deduplicates content and returns a bounded result list. The README documents vector, text, entity, type, tag, importance and relationship signals with text-only/vector-only fallback paths.

Memory operations are project-scoped in the documented host-facing paths: OpenCode binds its memory tools to the directory that registered the plugin, and Codex MCP operations require an explicit project identifier. A project search that finds no rows may retry against legacy rows with null project_id, but not another named project. Project identifiers are not authentication or hostile multi-tenant authorization; separate trust domains require separate databases and credentials.

Saved provenance can identify source kind, evidence strength, source session, agent, model and surface; CSM also documents evidence distinctions, source attribution and governance reports. Provenance completeness is audited, but evidence metadata does not make stored text safe or prove that a generated answer is supported.

The implementation has source-visible efficiency and operational surfaces, including parallel retrieval lanes, bounded results, provider-aware tool registration, recall telemetry and provenance-gap reports. These are implementation/documentation observations; this review collected no runtime latency, token, cost or storage measurements.

metrics.text: All project benchmark domains remain unmeasured for CSM because the system and benchmark workloads were not run. The fixture and METRICS.md define protocol, not CSM outcomes.

limits.text: The documented provider boundary is material: PostgreSQL supports the complete stack, while SQLite is a deliberately narrower core. Tool availability and features such as vector backfill, advanced governance, Living State analysis and context/checkpoint workflows differ by provider.

Project scoping is local data partitioning, not an identity or tenant authorization layer. Direct database credentials, SQLite filesystem access and unrestricted programmatic APIs have operator-wide reach; legacy null-project rows are migration data rather than a tenant boundary.

Redaction covers supported capture and storage boundaries but is not retroactive, cannot find every sensitive value and does not cover every field with the same end-to-end proof. CSM does not provide application-level field encryption, and deletion does not remove all downstream copies.

This is a bounded review of the README, product architecture, privacy/security documentation, memory manager, hybrid search, duplicate merger and provenance audit. It does not establish behavior for every tool, host, provider, migration, database query or deployment.
